content:
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data engineer with 9 years of experience building and operating batch and streaming data platforms across logistics, payments and retail. Experienced in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and cloud data warehouses, with a focus on reliable pipelines, data quality and dimensional modelling. AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 03/2022–Present
- Own ingestion and orchestration for the data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake. Participate in the platform on-call rotation, one week in six.
- Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to dbt, building over 420 models with tests on every model. Introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5h 10m to 1h 35m.
- Introduced data contracts using JSON Schema and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine to two per month.
- Designed and built a Kafka and Snowpipe Streaming pipeline for shipment events, processing approximately 30 million events per day with p95 end-to-end latency under two minutes. Added a dead-letter topic and replay tooling for failed events.
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
- Reduced monthly Snowflake costs by approximately 37% through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.
- Mentor two data engineers and run weekly data platform office hours.

Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 09/2019–02/2022
- Built PySpark reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files daily from S3. Automated matching of bank settlement files to internal ledgers, reducing finance's manual reconciliation work from approximately three days to four hours per month-end.
- Designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse with more than 30 fact and dimension tables used by finance and risk.
- Set up Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
- Developed an internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access, used by four teams.

Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | 06/2017–08/2019
- Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL for an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
- Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron, making loads easier to debug and change.
- Built Power BI reports for store operations across more than 40 stores.

SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data platforms: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations
Cloud and engineering: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions, CI/CD
Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, data contracts, data quality testing
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)

CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024

EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science, Data Science track | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries

OPEN SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
- Contributed two merged pull requests to a community Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests in Python.
- Teach beginner SQL at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since 2021.
- Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup in 2024.

LANGUAGES
Croatian: Native | English: C1 | German: B1

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior data engineering CV with clear progression, relevant technical breadth, and unusually effective quantified achievements. It demonstrates production ownership, platform scale, reliability, cost optimisation, data quality, mentoring, and open-source activity. The experience bullets are specific and credible, and the certification, community work, and English proficiency strengthen the profile. Minor opportunities remain to make the fit for a shared Data Platform role even more explicit, particularly around query optimisation, platform operations, and collaboration with analytics or product stakeholders.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, headers, or parsing obstacles. Strong matching terms include data platform, Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, Spark, Docker, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, data quality, and open source. AI screening probability is high because the document contains both relevant keywords and measurable evidence. To improve matching further, use the job ad's supported wording such as "production data platform," "cloud data warehouse," "query optimisation," and "platform operations" where the existing evidence supports those terms.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the role. It clearly shows experience designing, building, and operating a production data platform and cloud data warehouses at scale; AWS provides comparable cloud experience to Google Cloud; and the CV demonstrates Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, data quality, dimensional modelling, mentoring, and open-source contribution. The payments experience and reconciliation work are particularly relevant to Halden Pay. The platform's data contracts, CI checks, data quality tests, and office hours also support the company's Ownership, Together, and learning-oriented culture, without making unsupported cultural claims. The candidate's material does not show graph modelling or Portuguese, which are nice-to-have gaps. Query optimisation is supported indirectly through the dbt, incremental-model, warehouse-build, and Snowflake cost work, but the CV does not state it explicitly. Access-policy ownership and direct Google Cloud experience are not shown; AWS is the truthful comparable-cloud evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the opening to explicitly match the role's platform language while retaining only supported claims: "Data engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production batch and streaming data platforms and cloud data warehouses across logistics, payments and retail." Keep the existing technology and reliability sentence, and add: "Experienced in optimising large-scale warehouse workloads, data quality and dimensional modelling." This is supported by the 1.2 TB daily EMR workload, 30 million events per day, dbt build-time reduction, and Snowflake cost reduction.
2. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, revise the first bullet to make operational ownership more ATS-visible: "Own ingestion and orchestration for a production data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake; participate in the data-platform on-call rotation one week in six." This uses evidence already present in the candidate notes and improves alignment with the responsibility to run a central platform.
3. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, add the supported query-optimisation and scale evidence to the dbt or Snowflake bullet. For example, revise the dbt bullet to: "Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to dbt, building over 420 models with tests on every model; introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5h 10m to 1h 35m." Then revise the Snowflake bullet to: "Reduced monthly Snowflake costs by approximately 37% through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables." This makes the existing optimisation evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without claiming unsupported query techniques.
4. In the Skills section, change "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, data contracts, data quality testing" to "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling (star schema), data contracts, data quality testing, JSON Schema". The star-schema wording is supported by the Redshift warehouse experience, and JSON Schema is explicitly documented in the data-contract achievement.
5. In the Open Source and Community section, retain the Airflow provider contribution but include the technologies from the original candidate material: "Contributed two merged pull requests to a community Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding Python tests." This strengthens the job's open-source-practices match while remaining concise.
